issues.description: [bug-hunt] Notification auto-pause feature is dead code in production. update_auto_pause() (backend app/services/notification_service.py:410) is never called anywhere outside tests, so NotificationPreference.auto_paused is never set to True. Consequences: (1) the "Notifications paused / Resume Notifications" warning banner in src/pages/NotificationPreferences.tsx (gated on prefs.auto_paused, lines 285-305) NEVER renders - dead UI; (2) suppression Check 3 in send_notification (if prefs.auto_paused and trigger_source==scheduled, line 320) never fires, so a user who ignores 3+ consecutive scheduled pushes keeps getting nagged forever - the exact behavior the feature was built to prevent. EXPECTED: a nightly/post-send path calls update_auto_pause() per active user. ACTUAL: no call site and no APScheduler job exists (grep update_auto_pause across backend returns only tests; the scheduler block backend.py:15600-16230 has no auto-pause job). The reset path (reset_auto_pause wired to POST /notifications/:id/track-open) AND unit tests for update_auto_pause both exist, confirming the trigger was dropped, not intentionally omitted. REPRO: ignore every scheduled push for a week -> still receiving them; open /notification-preferences -> paused banner never appears. FIX: register a scheduled job (or call after sends) that runs update_auto_pause() for active users.

fix.description: Root cause: the on-device weekly weigh-in reminder used Capacitor weekday=1 (Sunday) while the backend push job fires Monday, so native users got two reminders on different days. Fix: set the local reminder to Monday (weekday=2) to match the backend weekly_weight_reminder job.

issues.author: shakeebshaan
issues.description: [bug-hunt] Weekly weigh-in reminder fires on TWO different days. The on-device LOCAL reminder is scheduled for SUNDAY while the backend PUSH job fires MONDAY. src/lib/reminderSync.ts DEFAULT_REMINDER_TIMES.weighIn.weekday = 1 (Capacitor Weekday enum: 1 = Sunday) is passed to scheduleWeeklyReminder(REMINDER_IDS.WEIGH_IN, weekday=1, ...) via applyProgressReminders -> local weigh-in reminder every SUNDAY 8am. But the backend job weekly_weight_reminder is registered CronTrigger(day_of_week=mon, hour=2, minute=30 UTC) = MONDAY 8am IST (backend.py:16214; job name literally "Weekly Weigh-in Reminder (Mon 8:00 AM IST)"). EXPECTED: one weigh-in reminder on a consistent day. ACTUAL: a native user with Progress Updates + push enabled gets a LOCAL nag Sunday 8am AND a backend PUSH Monday 8am. The FE comment weekday: 1 /* Sunday */ shows 1 was chosen deliberately as Sunday, contradicting the Monday product intent. FIX: set DEFAULT_REMINDER_TIMES.weighIn.weekday = 2 (Capacitor Monday) so the local reminder matches the backend job.

issues.description: [suggestion] Quick-add "Recent meals" row for one-tap re-logging of frequently eaten foods. Problem: meal logging (FoodSearchSheet) requires a full search+select+qty flow every time, even for the same dal/roti/protein-shake a user eats daily — the highest-frequency action in the app has the highest friction, which is a known churn driver in nutrition trackers (MyFitnessPal/Cronometer both ship "recent" and "favorites" as their #1 speed feature). Evidence: grepped src/pages/_components/nutrition + components/plan-builder — no favorites/recent/quick-add/log-again surface exists anywhere in the logging flow today. Proposed v1: backend endpoint returning the user’s last 8 distinct logged foods (query existing meal-log table, group by food_id, order by last-logged desc) + a "Recent" chip row atop FoodSearchSheet; tapping re-logs the same food/qty at current time via the existing log-meal endpoint (no new write path). Effort: ~1 backend endpoint (S) + ~1 FE component insert (S), no schema change — half-day.

issues.description: [suggestion] Injury-aware exercise substitution when a plan is paused for injury. Problem: PlanPauseScreen (src/pages/PlanPauseScreen.tsx) already has an "Injury" pause reason but only stores it as a label — no body-part capture and no downstream effect, so on resume the workout plan generator/coach can re-serve the exact movement that caused the injury (e.g. shoulder press after a shoulder injury). Evidence: REASONS array has injury as a flat enum value with no follow-up field; workout-plan generation and AI coach have no injury-exclusion input anywhere in the codebase. Comparable apps (Fitbod, Future) ask which body part and auto-avoid loading it. V1 scope: when reason=injury, show one extra step "Which area?" (shoulder/knee/back/wrist/ankle/other) + optional note; store on the pause record; on resume, pass the flagged body part(s) to the workout-plan builder/coach system prompt to exclude/soften exercises targeting that area for the first 1-2 weeks back, with a banner reminding the user to clear it manually if resolved sooner. Effort: ~1-2 days (1 new field + storage, 1 builder-prompt condition, 1 UI step).

issues.author: shakeebshaan
issues.reviewReason: Root cause found: the Daily Volume TARGET is not derived from today's plan at all. The app shows weekly_volume_target_kg / 7, and that weekly figure is last week's ACTUAL logged volume x1.05 (from backend /activity/overview). So the denominator has no relation to today's 11 exercises / 29 planned sets, which is why 2 exercises nearly fill it. Recommended fix (full-stack): backend adds planned_volume_today_kg = sum over today's exercises of target_sets x reps x reference_weight (reference weight proxied from each exercise's last logged set, since the plan stores no target weight); FE reads that instead of weekly/7. This changes what 'daily volume target' means (a product decision) and needs a backend deploy, so flagging for your call. Can implement next tick on approval.
